guide.title: Editor quick guide
guide.intro: Build and run a quantum circuit in a few steps, without writing code.

palette.title: Pick the blocks
palette.body: Drag gates from the palette on the left (Hadamard, CNOT, Measure…) onto the canvas. Right-click the canvas to search a block by name.

connect.title: Connect them in order
connect.body: Link one block's output to the next block's input. Connections set the order the operations run in.

properties.title: Tune the properties
properties.body: Select a block to choose its qubit, classical bit or number of shots in the side panel.

run.title: Finish with Run
run.body: Add Measure on the qubits, then Run (Aer Simulator) and, for the chart, Plot Histogram. Click ▶ to run.

console.title: Read the result
console.body: The Console tab shows output while the script runs and the histogram at the end. Use ■ to stop a long run.

save.title: Your work saves itself
save.body: The project is saved automatically. When it is ready, use Publish to Vault to share it.

guide.shortcuts: Shortcuts: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, Delete removes the selected block.

emptyCanvas.title: Your circuit starts here
emptyCanvas.subtitle: The canvas is empty. Start from a ready-made example or build your own:
emptyCanvas.step1: Drag blocks from the palette on the left onto here.
emptyCanvas.step2: Connect the blocks in the order they should run.
emptyCanvas.step3: Finish with Measure → Run and click ▶.
emptyCanvas.exampleHint: The Bell state entangles two qubits: the histogram shows only 00 and 11. Ctrl+Z undoes it.

home.title: Build quantum circuits by dragging blocks
home.subtitle: Node-Forge is a visual IDE for Qiskit: drag gates, connect them, click ▶ and see the result in seconds, with the Python code generated for you.
home.audience: Made for students and curious minds getting started with quantum computing.
home.sketchCaption: Bell state: the first circuit you run in the editor.

drag.title: Drag
drag.body: Pick quantum gates from the palette and drop them on the canvas.

connect.title: Connect
connect.body: Link the blocks in the order the operations happen.

run.title: Run
run.body: Click ▶: the circuit runs in an isolated simulator and the histogram shows up in the Console.

sandbox.title: Safe execution
sandbox.body: Every run happens in an isolated container, with no network and a time limit.

terminal.title: Python terminal
terminal.body: A real REPL, with your file's variables and functions already loaded.

results.title: Instant results
results.body: Script output while it runs and histograms at the end of every run.

vault.title: Node Vault
vault.body: Publish your circuits and clone the community's.
